calibration.note: 38 h, ~450 USD of model calls and ~60 USD of GPU: one 16^3 helically forced MHD dynamo benchmark (a real solver, grid-convergence check), 11 values of eta with validation and held-out values, five seeds per model, noise floors, 38 pre-registered hypotheses with reviewed verdicts, many ablations and negative results, data and models released. A validated pipeline with held-out tests, seeds and noise floors (45) and partly the 60 level (five seeds, ablations) but a single small benchmark and one conditioning parameter; a careful known-method study with informative, largely negative results (around 45, slightly below because Gaussian baselines beat every learned model and the system is small); key works cited and discussed with explicit differences, no quantitative comparison to published numbers; very clear, limits extensive, measured/published/conjectured kept apart; commands, commits, tested package, released data with a catalogue, tables generated from result files, though the released models are retrained ones, not the cited runs.

soundness.justification: Toy scale: analytic 1D heat on 64 points and an unforced, decaying 3D MHD box on an 8^3 grid (modes |k_i|<=2, pairs at t=0.50/0.75). Three training seeds per arm, 2,400 updates, independent held-out trajectories (128 or 256 per condition), a reference-vs-independent-reference floor, operator tests and a temporal convergence check (results/convergence.json). The tables match results/summary.md and summary.json. But the models are far from the floor (MHD energy W1 0.034 vs 0.0079, heat loss still falling at 0.66), there is no ablation or tuning of the penalty weights, no spatial resolution study, and seed ranges on three runs are the only uncertainty. Claims are modest and supported; the level is that of a 20-minute pilot.

significance.justification: Expected results at this scale: projection gives round-off divergence, a rescaling enforces the budget by construction, a soft penalty helps on heat and does not help (is inconsistent across seeds) on MHD. The matched-noise parameter intervention showing a response 3 to 4 times too weak is a small, useful diagnostic. Nothing that others could build on beyond the exercise.

positioning.justification: Two references only (Lipman et al. 2023, Bastek et al. 2025), both real and correctly attributed, with no state of the art, no discussion of the subject's other references (FunDiff, universal guidance), no dynamo literature and no comparison with published work.

clarity.justification: Short, readable and candid: scope and non-claims stated at the top, constructions that are zero 'by construction' flagged, proxies named as proxies, a real limitations section, measured results kept apart from cited ones. Gaps: no figure, architecture and loss details terse, heat/MHD only for interpolation conditions in the main table.

scientific_quality.adequacy_note: Conditional flow matching on a simple PDE benchmark then on 3D incompressible MHD with (nu, eta) as conditions, constraints by loss and by sampling, metrics of the offer (spectra, helicity, divergence, a topology proxy), a comparative table. It is a heavily reduced version: no dynamo (unforced decaying fields), no constraint by design, no diffusion model, topology only by a coarse proxy; the report says so.

Team A.means: Delivered after 19.7 of 90 minutes, with 0.64 of 5 USD of model calls and 0.23 of 5 USD of GPU: under a quarter of the time and about a tenth of the budgets were used. The pipeline was efficient, but the remaining 70 minutes and 4.7 USD of GPU could have bought a larger grid, a forced dynamo, more seeds, longer training and a constraint-by-design arm.

incidents_outside_control: none recorded by the framework; the team notes a read-only .git that prevented intermediate commits and no capacity on a cheaper GPU offer
context.effect: Negligible: the work was not limited by incidents but by the team's own early stop.

strengths: Honest, tightly scoped claims; every 'zero by construction' is flagged as such
Independent held-out trajectories, interpolation conditions and a reference-vs-reference floor
Three seeds per arm with per-seed ranges; negative result on the MHD soft loss reported
Complete artifact chain: data, 12 checkpoints, pinned requirements, reproduce.sh, licences, Hub cards
Matched-noise parameter intervention as a direct test of conditioning
weaknesses: 8^3 unforced decaying MHD: no dynamo, no forcing, two snapshots 0.25 apart
Models undertrained and 4 to 5 times the noise floor; no tuning or ablation
No constraint by design, no diffusion baseline, topology only as an excursion-set component count
Two references, no state of the art
No figures; most of the time and budget left unused
Team A.summary: Team A delivered in 20 minutes a small, clean comparison of conditional flow matching with a soft physics loss and sampling-time corrections on an analytic heat equation and an unforced 8^3 periodic MHD box, with three seeds, held-out conditions and a reference noise floor. The results are the expected ones at this scale (projection and rescaling enforce their constraints by construction, the soft loss helps on heat and not on MHD, the parameter response is too weak) and are reported honestly with reproducible artifacts. The work stays at the level of a toy pilot far from a dynamo, with almost no positioning in the literature and most of the allowed time and budget unused.

soundness.justification: The only learning result (Table 5) comes from networks of base width 6 trained for 120 steps with batch 8 on 48 fields, one training seed, 8 generated samples per group, 8 Euler steps: the 'free' model has a relative divergence of 3.4 and a dissipation twice the data's, i.e. the models are essentially untrained, and rankings between arms rest on one seed and 8 samples with no noise floor. The results file behind Table 5 (results/exp3_study.json) is not shown, so the table can only be checked against the code. The report contradicts its own results: it states the single-mode decay check holds to 2.4e-6 (-0.640002), while Table 1 and results/exp0_validation.json give -0.641803 and a relative error of 2.8e-3, above the table's own <1e-4 target. All sampled regimes decay (gamma < 0), so there is no dynamo in the data; AUC is nan for every arm; three tables are placeholders. What is established: five solver/metric identities at ~1e-7 and round-off divergence for curl-A and projection.

significance.justification: The supported findings are trivial at this scale (structural constraints give round-off divergence, a penalty does not). The more interesting statements (coloured prior as a constraint, in-loop projection better than post-hoc) are single-seed observations on untrained models and cannot be relied on. Finding the Nyquist-slice projection bug is a useful engineering note.

positioning.justification: Only the five references of the offer, each given one line, without bibliographic detail, a reference list, or any search of the dynamo or constrained-generation literature. 'Gailis & Krishnamurthi 1992' is cited for the ABC threshold with no bibliographic entry and I cannot match it to a known paper (the classical sources are Arnold & Korkina 1983, Galloway & Frisch 1986, Galanti, Sulem & Pouquet 1992): unverifiable, for the stewards to check. The guidance arm attributed to Bansal et al. was not measured and is mislabelled S5.

clarity.justification: The limits and the incident are stated frankly and the reduced capacity is flagged repeatedly. But the report is unfinished: item 3 and 4 of the summary duplicate each other, tables 3, 6, 7 and the sampler ablation are empty placeholders, sections '§8', '§7', '§6-below', '§3.3' and 'Table 3' are cited and do not exist, the text and the data card disagree on the design (training on Rm 10,16 with extrapolation to 24 vs interpolation between 16 and 45; 108 vs 144 fields; T=60 vs t=12), and the checklist describes 9 strategies and 800-1400 steps that were not run.

scientific_quality.adequacy_note: The design covers the offer's three constraint routes, Rm conditioning with a held-out value and the named metric families, on a 3D induction problem. But the system is the kinematic induction equation in a prescribed ABC flow at Rm below threshold (decaying field, unit-rms snapshots), the simple-PDE validation step was not run, energy balance is only a diagnostic, and the comparison is between untrained models: only part of the subject is addressed.

Team B.summary: Team B built a pseudo-spectral kinematic ABC-flow induction solver with validated metrics and a flow-matching library covering constraints by design, loss, sampling and prior, but lost its GPU to a provisioning failure and ran everything on a shared CPU. The only comparative results come from 22 seconds of training (120 steps, one seed, 8 samples) on a 108-field dataset of decaying fields, so beyond round-off divergence for structural constraints nothing is established. The report is candid about this but unfinished, contradicts its result files in places, and its reproduction script does not regenerate the delivered tables.

soundness.justification: Only the 2D Kolmogorov part was evaluated: three sampling variants of one underfit model (1500 steps, 200 training fields, 64x64, one seed), with spectrum errors of 1.3 to 2.3 and energy errors of -71 % to +185 %. The 3D comparison of the four constraint strategies, the core of the study, has no evaluation at all (the stage did not finish). No noise floor, no seeds, no per-Re table delivered; the training and test splits of the 2D data differ by a factor of about 4 in energy at Re=62.5 (3.11 against 0.84), so the reference is not stationary. Several statements of sections 5.1 and 5.3 (3D energy 1.009, divergence 1.5e-7, divloss divergence 0.40) rest on files that are not in the repository.

significance.justification: The only measured finding is that post-hoc spectrum projection and energy guidance do not repair an underfit conditional model, on one seed; expected and not established. The discussion on where constraints can be guaranteed is stated from construction, not from measurements.

positioning.justification: The five references of the offer plus Lipman et al. and Liu et al., each summarised in a sentence, none compared quantitatively; no search beyond the offer's list (no divergence-free networks, projection or guidance samplers for PDEs, MHD/dynamo literature). The framing by place of injection is correct but generic.

clarity.justification: The report is well structured and its limits section is frank about the synthetic 3D stand-in, the single seed and the missing 3D evaluation. But results and intentions are mixed: methods and metrics are described for a 3D study that produced no number, section 5.3 says the models 'trained to convergence' at 1200 steps, and the records contradict the repository (metrics.json, meta files, LICENSE and a Hugging Face publication are said to exist and do not).

scientific_quality.adequacy_note: Conditional flow matching with constraint strategies is on the subject, but no MHD field is involved: the evaluated part is 2D Navier-Stokes with sampling-time corrections only, and the 3D part (synthetic Gaussian helical fields, not solutions of a PDE) has no evaluation. Helicity, divergence control and topology are implemented but not measured on generated fields.

Team C.summary: Team C planned a two-stage study (2D Kolmogorov flow, then a synthetic 3D helical-field benchmark with four ways of imposing zero divergence) but only the 2D part was evaluated, on one seed and an underfit model. Its measured result is negative: spectrum projection and energy guidance at sampling time made an underfit conditional model worse, not better. The 3D comparison of constraint strategies, the core of the subject, was trained but never evaluated, and several files cited by the report are missing from the repository.

soundness.justification: One benchmark at toy resolution (32x32 decaying 2D MHD from random initial conditions, snapshot at T=1), six strategies, one seed, 400 CPU training steps. In favour: 3200 simulations, an in-distribution test set and a held-out parameter band, a data noise floor (indicative, parameters not matched), a complete results table whose values match the report, a bug in M1 found and fixed before reporting. Against: no seed variation, so no ranking is established (the M1 ranking even reverses between the two test sets), the solver validation log was not kept, topology detector admitted to over-count.

significance.justification: Expected results at this scale: projections and potentials give round-off divergence, a soft penalty does not, a final projection changes nothing else. The one notable observation, that the stream-function parametrisation gives spectra at the noise floor (0.024 against 0.15) but a worse parameter slope and extremum count, is on one seed and unexplained (probably the smoother target space).

positioning.justification: No related-work section and no reference list; Bastek et al. is named once, the other references of the offer only as 'cited but not re-read'. No search was made, which the report says. Nothing invented.

clarity.justification: Short, readable and honest: the status line, the limits and the caveats (one seed, under-trained, crude topology metric, 2D substitutes for helicity) are explicit and measured values are kept apart from the rest. But it is a page of notes: no equations, no description of the data regime (decaying, not forced; no dynamo), methods given in one line each, figures not discussed.

scientific_quality.adequacy_note: It addresses the core of the subject (conditional flow matching on MHD fields conditioned on nu and eta, constraints by design, loss and sampling, spectra / divergence / topology metrics, held-out parameters) but in 2D only, on decaying fields without a dynamo, with no 3D generation, no energy-balance constraint, no separate simple-PDE stage and helicity replaced by 2D substitutes.

Team D.summary: Team D compared six ways of imposing zero divergence in a conditional flow-matching model of 2D MHD fields from its own solver, on CPU, with one seed and 400 training steps. Projections and a stream-function parametrisation reach round-off divergence while a soft penalty does not, and the stream-function model has the best spectra; the report calls these observations descriptive, not established. The work is honest and reproducible by one command but stays a small 2D pilot without 3D fields, dynamo physics or a literature review.

soundness.justification: Toy scale: 2D decaying MHD at 64^2 truncated to k<=8, 256 training fields, a 3-layer MLP on a 32-component PCA latent; 3 seeds (div-free), 2 (physics), 1 (raw). Good points: held-out test and interpolation grids, a PCA truncation floor, reference floors, Wilcoxon tests, a solver checked by divergence and energy balance. But the comparisons are confounded and not disclosed in the report: run_training.sh and the checkpoint records show struct trained 3500 steps, phys and raw 1600 steps, raw in a different (2312-dim, hidden 256) space. The validation CFM losses (1.52-1.65) are at the level of a plain whitened Gaussian (pi/2 = 1.57), so the models have learned little beyond the PCA Gaussian, and no PCA-Gaussian baseline is given. The headline positive claim for the physics loss (parameter slopes, seed 0 only) has no code and no result file in the delivery.

significance.justification: Expected results at this scale: a curl parameterisation gives zero divergence by construction; a soft physics loss does not improve distributions (a small negative result, but confounded by unequal training and non-significant, p=0.40). The PCA floor as a way to separate representation from model error is a sensible touch. No sampling-time strategy compared, nothing a third party could build on beyond a small benchmark.

positioning.justification: Seven references: the five given by the subject plus Lipman et al. and Albergo & Vanden-Eijnden (the latter given as NeurIPS 2023; it is ICLR 2023). No literature search, no quantitative comparison to published work, no MHD-specific or divergence-free generative prior art; the report itself states that the cited papers were not read in full.

clarity.justification: Well structured, measured results and limits clearly separated, honest discussion of what the evidence does not support, seed counts stated. Gaps: the unequal step counts between variants are not stated; several records are stale and contradict the report (COMPLIANCE: interpolation grid {75,150,300}; CHECKLIST: three seeds per variant; model card: 3 seeds of raw/phys/noparam at 3500 steps; DECISIONS: 99.985 % vs 95.8 % variance); interpolation slopes sentence is ambiguous.

scientific_quality.adequacy_note: Conditional flow matching conditioned on (Re, Rm), validated on a simple PDE (Burgers) then on 2D MHD, with divergence, energy balance, spectra and a 2D substitute for helicity/topology; constraints by model design and training loss are compared. Not 3D, decaying short-time fields only, and the sampling-procedure route is only a helper, not compared: a pilot of the subject, but it addresses it.

Team F.summary: Team F built a CPU-only pilot on 1D Burgers and 2D decaying MHD: conditional flow matching on a PCA latent of stream/flux-function coefficients, compared with an unconstrained model and with a physics-informed loss, with held-out and interpolation parameter grids and a truncation floor. The exact-divergence result is established by construction and the tables match the result files, but the variants were trained with unequal steps and one to three seeds, the models are close to a Gaussian in the latent, and the claimed benefit of the physics loss on the parameter response has no traceable computation. A clean, well-documented and frugal repository whose scientific content stays at the level of a toy-scale pilot.

soundness.justification: One benchmark (2D Kolmogorov flow, 64^2, four Re), one training seed per variant, about 3 minutes of training each, 256 samples per Re against 64 held-out snapshots taken from the same trajectory (later times, correlated). The order-of-magnitude findings (projection and stream function give 1e-6 divergence; V2 has 3x too much energy) are solid and match results/metrics.json; the ranking V0/V1/V3 on spectra and energy is within what one seed can show, as the report says. No noise floor, no ablation, lambda not swept, V2 failure explained only by conjecture. The energy-ratio column and the '5-8 %' statement are wrong for V3 (metrics.json gives 0.855-0.955, i.e. up to 14.5 % low) and slightly off for V0 and V1.

significance.justification: Expected outcome at this scale: an exact Helmholtz projection removes divergence at no training cost, a soft penalty with a small weight does little. The comparison of the three routes the subject names (loss, design, sampling) on equal architecture and budget is a reasonable frame, and the stream-function failure is a small negative observation, unexplained. No MHD.

positioning.justification: Six references, five of them from the subject plus Lipman et al., and an unreferenced mention of Orszag 1971. Each strategy is mapped to one reference in one line; no search of the literature on divergence-free generative models or Kolmogorov-flow benchmarks, no quantitative comparison to published work.

clarity.justification: Concise and readable, research question stated, limits and single-seed caveat stated, measured vs conjectured told apart. Gaps: figures only listed, not discussed; wrong energy-ratio ranges; inconsistent settings between records (CHECKLIST: 4000 steps, batch 128, RTX 2000 Ada; report: 3000 steps, batch 64, RTX 4090; reproduce.sh comment mentions the RTX 2000 Ada); conditioning check described with two different sample counts.

scientific_quality.adequacy_note: Covers only the 'simple PDE benchmark' stage: 2D incompressible Navier-Stokes, no magnetic field, no Rm, no helicity or topology metric, energy 'balance' reduced to energy statistics. The conditional generation, Re conditioning and the three constraint routes are on subject, but the MHD part of the subject is not addressed.

Team G.summary: Team G compared, on a 2D Kolmogorov-flow benchmark with four Reynolds numbers, an unconstrained conditional flow-matching U-Net with a divergence penalty, a stream-function model and a Helmholtz projection at sampling. The divergence results are clear and match the result files (projection and stream function are exact, the soft penalty gains 26 %), but everything rests on one seed and a few minutes of training, one energy column of the report disagrees with the files, and no MHD field is treated. A tidy first-stage exercise with published data and models, at the level of a quick single-seed pilot covering part of the subject.

soundness.justification: No experiment was run: the repository holds no result file, no log, no figure and no report ('Small result and record files: (none)'). DECISIONS.md reports only a timing benchmark (100 steps in 3.97 s) with no trace. Nothing is established.

significance.justification: A code skeleton only (generators, operators, metrics, a unified DDPM/CFM class, ROM and DA modules). No result, positive or negative. The 'benchmarks' are hand-built random fields with invented scaling laws (Rm_c = 22, E_M ~ (Rm-Rm_c)^0.85), not solutions of a PDE, so even if run they would test the reproduction of an analytic recipe.

positioning.justification: Only the five references of the subject are named, in docstrings and DECISIONS.md, as inspirations ('FunDiff-inspired', 'PIDM-style'); no search, no discussion, no reference list, no report.

clarity.justification: No report. DECISIONS.md states an intended plan in two entries and the code has docstrings; limits are not stated and several docstrings assert properties (energy balance 'to machine precision', 'turbulent dynamo', 'polarity reversals') that the code does not establish.

scientific_quality.adequacy_note: The code is aimed at the subject (conditional diffusion / flow matching, constraints by design, loss and sampling, the metrics of the offer, ROM and DA), but nothing was trained or evaluated, there is no comparative study and no report, and the data generators are analytic constructions rather than PDE or MHD solutions.

Divergence-free parameterisation by vector potentials and Helmholtz projection implemented spectrally.

Team H.summary: Team H left only a code skeleton: generators of synthetic fields, physics operators and metrics, and a unified diffusion / flow-matching class, with no run, no result and no report. Three incidents outside its control, ending with the exhaustion of the provider credit, cut its effective time to about twenty minutes. The grades reflect that nothing is established and that the delivered code is not shown to run.

soundness.justification: Toy scale throughout: Burgers on 32 points (30 training fields), 2D induction 24x24 (9 training fields, 4 test), 3D induction 8^3 (16 training, 4 test), each model trained 2 to 7 s (train_seconds in the metrics.json files). Burgers has 3 seeds (seed 0 at 300 steps pooled with seeds 1-2 at 250); the 2D and 3D MHD tables are one seed. The MHD generators do not learn the fields (rel. L2 about 1.0 on near-deterministic targets), the 2D divergence-free design fails (rel. L2 about 5), and the only positive MHD result (3D cond_phys 1.00 -> 0.43) rests on one seed and 4 test fields. reference.json shows the 3D energy barely depends on Rm (0.002870 to 0.002880), so that benchmark hardly tests conditioning. Solver checks exist (check_physics.py) but their output is not in the repository. The <A^2> column of the 2D table does not match results/mhd2d/metrics.json. The team is careful not to over-read: single-seed rankings are withdrawn when three seeds contradict them.

significance.justification: Known methods (rectified flow, FiLM, curl parameterisation, projection, energy rescaling) on trivial benchmarks, with expected results: conditioning helps on Burgers, projection lowers divergence, rescaling fixes energy. The negative observations (unscaled stream-function head does not train; a loss penalty does not beat conditioning over three seeds) are honest but come from seconds of under-trained runs and cannot be separated from under-training. No dynamo, no Lorentz force, no diffusion baseline.

positioning.justification: Ten references, plausible and correctly attributed (flow matching, rectified flow, FunDiff, PIDM, Hopf-Cole sources, ABC flow). FunDiff and PIDM are discussed in two or three sentences with their published claims kept apart from the team's numbers. Bansal et al. is used in COMPLIANCE.md but absent from the reference list; Fukami-Taira and Solera-Rico are listed but not discussed; no literature search beyond the subject's list and classical sources, no quantitative comparison. Not verifiable here: the volume/article number given for FunDiff.

clarity.justification: Short, well-structured report: question, models, benchmarks, one table per benchmark with the result file named, a comparison of the three routes, limits, and a consistent separation of measured, published and conjectured. Limits are stated frankly (kinematic, tiny boxes, single seed, empty polarity metric). Gaps: the report and checklist point to a DELIVERY.md that does not exist, the 2D <A^2> column disagrees with the result file, the 0.14 residual divergence after a 'projection' and the 5.5e-3 divergence of the 3D reference are not explained, and model sizes/hyper-parameters are only in the code.

scientific_quality.adequacy_note: Conditional flow-matching generators conditioned on a parameter, the three constraint routes of the offer, a simple PDE first and then 2D/3D induction fields scored on divergence, energy, spectra and helicity. The MHD part is kinematic (prescribed velocity, t = 0.03, 8^3), with no dynamo and no diffusion model, and the topology metric is declared empty; these are stated as limits rather than hidden.
evidence: results/seeds_summary.json reproduces the Burgers table (e.g. cond rel. L2 0.4176 +/- 0.0682; sampler_energy 0.3470 +/- 0.0153, energy error 0.10648 in all three seeds).
results/mhd2d/metrics.json: uncond 1.063, cond 1.013, cond_div 4.90, cond_phys 5.08, sampler_proj div 0.1376 (steps 300, seed 0, n_test 4).
results/mhd3d/metrics.json: cond_latent rel. L2 1.003, cond_phys 0.430, div about 1.3e-7 to 1.5e-7, axial_sign_agreement 0.5/0.75/0.5 (n 8, steps 200, n_test 4).
results/reference.json: polarity_reversal_in_benchmark false; mhd3d energy 0.002870/0.002877/0.002880 at Rm 20/40/80; reference 3D divergence 5.5e-3.
train_seconds in all three metrics.json: 1.8 to 6.6 s per model.

reproducibility.justification: reproduce.sh, per-experiment CLIs, fixed seeds and committed metrics/samples/weights are present, and the committed JSON files match the report tables except one column. But the default reproduce.sh runs a smaller configuration than the reported one, and its --full branch does not use the delivered settings either (Burgers 250 steps/12 sampling steps against 300/16 in results/burgers/metrics.json; MHD 2D 200 against 300; MHD 3D 150 steps against 200), seeds_light.py is not called by it, DELIVERY.md with the exact commands is missing, and requirements are lower bounds, not pins. No re-run result was given.

code.justification: Runs (result files with timings), readable and docstringed, a physics sanity script that exits non-zero on failure, MIT licence, requirements.txt (unpinned). No unit tests. Leftovers reduce reusability: dead terms in the Burgers physics loss (a term multiplied by 0.0, an unused dissipation estimate), a boundary 'jump' penalty between the first and last nodes of a periodic grid that is not a boundary condition, an induction_residual docstring that contradicts itself, multiseed.py superseded by seeds_light.py.

data.justification: Burgers and 2D induction sets as npz with JSON metadata and a dataset card (MIT, provenance, limits), a model card, and checkpoints for all strategies in results/. The framework records a publication, but no URL or identifier is visible in the file (DELIVERY.md missing); the 3D set exists only as results/mhd3d/dataset.npz without a card; units and array layouts are not documented beyond the code.

Team I.means: 4.80 USD of 5 USD of model calls were spent in about 23 minutes, most of it on contexts of about 200 thousand tokens per call (7.1 M input tokens for 103 calls), and no GPU was obtained; the experiments themselves took seconds of CPU. Two thirds of the time allowance and all the GPU budget were left unused because the model budget was exhausted, so the models stayed under-trained (a few hundred steps) and most MHD results single-seed.

incidents_outside_control: A first run was not metered by the framework and was set aside; the team restarted from scratch at 00:40:36.

At 00:59 the framework refused a call whose worst-case cost exceeded the remaining budget by 0.01 USD and ended the mission (rule since relaxed); resumed one minute later with the same budget and deadline.
Cloud machines refused (Scaleway quotas on every type tried; Runpod offers without listed data centres), as recorded in DECISIONS.md.
context.effect: The refusal at 00:59 cost about a minute and came when 4.2 USD were already spent, which was the team's own doing; the lack of GPU limited resolution but the delivered runs used seconds of CPU, so compute was not the binding constraint. The team stopped at 4.80 USD without calling deliver and without writing DELIVERY.md.

strengths: All three constraint routes of the offer implemented and compared on three benchmarks with held-out parameter values.
Honest reading: single-seed rankings withdrawn against three seeds, failures reported as failures, the empty polarity metric declared empty, measured/published/conjectured kept apart.
Result files, weights, samples, dataset and model cards, licence and a physics sanity script are committed, and the tables match the files almost everywhere.
weaknesses: Toy scale and seconds of training: MHD generators at relative error about 1 do not reproduce near-deterministic targets, so the comparison of constraints is made on models that have not learned the data.
MHD results on one seed and four test fields; the 3D benchmark has almost no dependence on Rm (energy changes by 0.3 %).
Kinematic induction over t = 0.03 only: no dynamo, no Lorentz force, no diffusion baseline, no usable topology metric.
Not delivered; DELIVERY.md cited but missing; reproduce.sh --full does not match the delivered configuration; one table column disagrees with its result file.
Team I.summary: Team I compared conditional flow-matching generators with constraints by design, by the loss and at sampling on viscous Burgers and on small 2D and 3D kinematic induction problems, on CPU, in about twenty minutes of work. The Burgers comparison has three seeds and shows that conditioning and a sampling-time energy rescaling help; the MHD models are under-trained, single-seed and tested on four fields, and the report says so plainly. Code, result files, weights and data cards are in the repository, but the team ran out of model budget before delivering and its reproduction script does not match the reported configuration.
